title: Ready For Review - [Mouse Jump] - new border style, performance enhancements #50462, #50464

review.body_prefix:
### Qualified current-revision assessment

The new revision addresses the earlier actionable concerns: pointer activation is handled explicitly; startup no longer shows the invisible preview; user dismissal really hides the HWND; and the async event loop keeps listening while an invocation runs, cancelling and awaiting a superseded invocation before starting another.

Overlapping rounded screen bounds now use first-match hit testing instead of throwing on multiple matches. The border host is hit-testable and handles right-click dismissal, while pane clicks are marked handled. The UI test now waits for the region to be revealed after foreground activation, and normal show/hide transitions are restored. The dormant message-window helper now uses the executable module base address and disposes its Process wrapper.

These corrections remove the previously proposed comments. The added first-frame wait is bounded, unsubscribes its rendering handler in a finally block, and observes cancellation before revealing the region. No further demonstrated defect is established by this current-scope reassessment.

**Validation scope:** The complete delta within all 78 current PR files was read, including the new sync/async event-loop split, visibility/cancellation paths, generated DwmFlush wrapper and UI-test wait. This is source-level validation of the corrections. No new WinUI build, real rapid-hotkey/capture run, focus restoration experiment or mixed-DPI UI execution was performed; earlier checks retain their original revision identities. This is not an unconditional approval or UI signoff.
